chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Al-Khashaab, from Ali ibn Hassan, from one of our companions, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Feed the one suffering from stomach ailments rice bread, for nothing that enters the stomach of the one suffering from stomach ailments is more beneficial than it; indeed, it tans (strengthens) the stomach and pulls out the illness with a pull.'

key_terms.الْمَبْطُونَ: One suffering from stomach ailments or indigestion
key_terms.يَدْبُغُ: Tans or strengthens (referring to the stomach lining)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended treatment for stomach ailments according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the medicinal superiority of rice bread (*khubz al-aruzz*) for treating gastrointestinal disorders, describing it as a potent remedy that 'tans' or toughens the stomach lining. This recommendation reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating practical dietary advice with spiritual and physical healing, emphasizing the prophetic practice of using simple, natural foods for preventative care. The metaphor of 'tanning' suggests a process of strengthening and preserving the stomach against decay and disease.
